solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Picture suddenly changes, torrid

blocks.note: a mood or temper that snaps changes all at once
torrid weather is very hot

explanation.surface: Someone's view of a picture shifts abruptly, perhaps because the scene in it is steamy.
explanation.definitionFit: A snapshot is an informal photograph taken quickly, and a photograph is a kind of picture.

clue.text: Fashion range with dark clothes

indicators.note: to fashion something is to shape or make it, so the following words are remade into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A fashion house launches a collection of sombre clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dark clothes' reads as black garments, but it means clothes worn in the dark of night.
explanation.definitionFit: Nightwear is pyjamas and nighties, garments put on for bed after the sun has set.

clue.text: Particular types journalist introduced to rubbish

indicators.note: one thing introduced to another is put inside it, so the first piece goes within the second

blocks.note: pants is British slang for something rubbish or worthless
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: Certain kinds of reporter are dismissed as no good.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Particular' is an adjective in the surface but here is a noun sense: people who are fussy. Pants is British slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Pedants are fussy people obsessed with small details, the sort described as particular about rules.

clue.text: Egyptian God has shown strain, wiping brow

indicators.note: the brow is the top of a head, so wiping it off removes the word's opening letter

blocks.note: a strain is a passage of song, as a chorus is

explanation.surface: A sweating Egyptian deity shows effort and mops his forehead.
explanation.definitionFit: Horus is the falcon-headed sky deity of ancient Egypt, son of Isis and Osiris.

clue.text: Small boat at the same time capsized

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is overturned, and in a down clue that turns the word bottom to top

blocks.note: but, as in 'cheap but good', concedes something holding at the same time

explanation.surface: Several small boats overturn simultaneously.
explanation.definitionFit: A tub is informal for a slow, clumsy or small vessel, often a rowing boat.

clue.text: Envisage about month in retreat, for break away

indicators.note: an army in retreat moves backwards, so the month is written back to front
about means around, so the first word wraps the other

blocks.note: to envisage something is to see it in the mind
DEC is the calendar abbreviation for December

explanation.surface: Someone imagines retreating for a month to take a break.
explanation.definitionFit: To secede is for a state or region to withdraw formally from a union or federation.

clue.text: Drunk sounding mean — something in cocktail?

indicators.note: this is the word as slurred by someone drunk, turning the s sound into sh

blocks.note: mean means selfish, and a drunk says it with a slur

explanation.surface: A tipsy drinker sounds stingy while asking what is in the cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: A drunk slurs 'selfish' into 'shellfish'. The cocktail is a prawn cocktail, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Prawns are shellfish, and they are the main ingredient of a prawn cocktail starter.

clue.text: Dude impressed by plain entertainment

indicators.note: something impressed by another has that pressed into it, so the second word sits inside the first

blocks.note: a cat is old jazz slang for a cool guy
plain and bare both mean unadorned

explanation.surface: A city slicker is won over by a simple show.
explanation.definitionFit: Cabaret is a show of songs, dancing and comedy staged in a nightclub or restaurant.

clue.text: Published papers sent up for cash in Iraq

indicators.note: sent up in a down clue means moved upwards, so the letters read from the bottom

blocks.note: a newspaper that ran a story published it
ID means identity papers

explanation.surface: Published papers are ridiculed in exchange for money in Iraq.
explanation.definitionFit: The dinar is the currency unit of Iraq, as of several other Arab countries.

clue.text: Get away from electronic gadget? Well, once!

indicators.note: to get away from something is to leave it, so these letters are taken out of what follows

blocks.note: E is the standard abbreviation for electronic, as in e-mail
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone urges escape from an electronic device, with an old-fashioned exclamation.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening 'Get' is not an instruction to the solver: it is the three letters to remove.
explanation.definitionFit: Egad is an archaic mild oath of surprise, so it is what people once said for 'well!'.

clue.text: Stretcher in match forbidden, did you say?

indicators.note: asking what someone said points to a word that is heard rather than seen

blocks.note: a rubber is a match of several games in bridge or cricket
forbidden means banned, said aloud

explanation.surface: A medic queries whether stretchers are banned during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stretcher' suggests a medical carrier; here it is something that stretches.
explanation.definitionFit: A rubber band is an elastic loop that stretches around things to hold them together.

clue.text: Drawer opened by bears — jam!

blocks.note: to bear something is to stand it, tolerate it
a till is the cash drawer in a shop

explanation.surface: A drawer is pried open by bears looking for jam.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Opened by' puts the second piece at the front. 'Jam' suggests something to spread, but it is traffic gridlock.
explanation.definitionFit: A traffic jam brings vehicles to a complete halt, a state of no movement whatever.

clue.text: Moving through letters, I’ve arrived at “P” for ‘Paint‘?

blocks.note: sets the scene: stepping through the alphabet one letter at a time
read as I am, contracted to I'm
to arrive at P in the alphabet is to be past O

explanation.surface: Someone working through the alphabet has reached the letter for Paint.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as I'M PAST O: when you reach P in the alphabet you have gone past O.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is paint laid on so thickly that brush or knife strokes stand out on the canvas.

clue.text: Infrequent choice

blocks.note: first meaning: seldom occurring
second meaning: excellent, of top quality

explanation.walkthrough: 'Choice' looks like a noun but is the adjective meaning select, as in choice cuts.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both uncommon in occurrence and unusually fine, as with a prized vintage.

clue.text: Possible target of bowler set back by defeat

indicators.note: set back here means written backwards, read from the end to the beginning

blocks.note: jelly that sets is said to gel
a problem that stumps you defeats you

explanation.surface: A bowler suffers a setback in defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: The bowler is a cricketer, not a hat or a ten-pin player. In cricket, the bowler aims at three upright stumps behind the batsman.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg stump is the stump on the batsman's leg side, one of three the bowler tries to hit.

clue.text: Adequate university top after review: put out

indicators.note: a review revisits and reorganises something, so this word comes out in a new order

blocks.note: U is the standard abbreviation
taken as written
to snuff a candle is to put it out

explanation.surface: A university head, after a poor assessment, is upset.
explanation.definitionFit: Up to snuff is an idiom for meeting the required standard, good enough.

clue.text: Determined, living outdoors?

definitions.note: the second reading is the phrase IN TENT

blocks.note: first meaning: resolved, set on doing something
second meaning, split in two: camping under canvas

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second meaning: read the answer as IN TENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone intent on a goal is fixed and resolved; a camper sleeps in a tent outdoors.

clue.text: Silent left-hander’s initial punches I sense, so brutal

indicators.note: the initial of a word is its first letter
a punch goes into its target, so this letter is driven inside the other letters
brutal treatment knocks things about, so these words are battered into a new order

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A southpaw boxer quietly lands a savage blow, it seems to me.
explanation.walkthrough: The left-hander suggests a boxer, which makes 'punches' look literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Noiseless means making no sound at all, exactly what silent describes.

clue.text: Paid model brings good luck to drinker

blocks.note: a pro, professional, is paid
an artist's model sits for a portrait

explanation.surface: A paid model brings fortune to someone at the bar.
explanation.definitionFit: Prosit is a German and Latin toast wishing health, said when raising glasses before drinking.

clue.text: Water turning coach upside down? Correct

indicators.note: turned upside down in a down clue, the word reads from bottom to top
turning round puts this word back to front as well

blocks.note: a coach is a long-distance bus
the tide is the rise and fall of sea water

explanation.surface: Floodwater overturns a coach.
explanation.definitionFit: To subedit is to check and correct copy before it goes into a newspaper.

clue.text: Solid lead blocking sinks from behind

indicators.note: read from behind means starting at the end, so the word is reversed
something blocking a passage sits in the middle of it

blocks.note: something that sinks dips
the lead in a film is its hero

explanation.surface: A lump of lead clogs the kitchen sinks from the back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' suggests the metal, and 'solid' and 'sinks' egg it on, but it is the leading role.
explanation.definitionFit: A spheroid is a solid figure shaped roughly like a sphere, in geometry a three-dimensional shape.

clue.text: Mutton neck, odd bits gone in dish

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters gone, only the even ones remain

blocks.note: mutton is sheep meat, and a ram is a male sheep
the second and fourth letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mutton neck is served in a dish once the stray scraps are trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: A ramekin is a small ovenproof bowl used for baking and serving individual portions.

clue.text: Card game, cheat

blocks.note: first meaning: short for cribbage
second meaning: to copy someone else's work

explanation.walkthrough: Cribbage is a card game scored on a pegboard; crib is its usual short name.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib names a card game and also the verb for copying answers dishonestly in an exam.

clue.text: Animal with horn, I suspect

indicators.note: suspect as an adjective means dubious or not right, so the letters are wrongly ordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone guesses that a beast bearing a horn is in view.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer, since a rhino has a horn.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhinoceros is a large African or Asian beast, so it is one example of an animal.

clue.text: Rider put garment on display

indicators.note: one thing put on another in the clue goes after it here, so the garment follows the display

blocks.note: a display is a show
a jumper is British for a sweater

explanation.surface: A rider puts a piece of clothing on view.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put on' suggests getting dressed, but the garment is placed after the display.
explanation.definitionFit: A showjumper rides a horse over a course of fences in competition, so is an equestrian.

clue.text: Ever so happy

blocks.note: first meaning: very, in British speech
second meaning: cheerful, merry

explanation.walkthrough: In British English jolly is an informal intensifier, as in 'jolly good'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word serves as a chatty British adverb for very and an adjective for merry or cheerful.

clue.text: Where aircraft tested, turn north into air, then left

indicators.note: going into something means being placed inside it

blocks.note: to wind a key is to turn it
an air is a melody
N is the compass abbreviation
L is the usual abbreviation

explanation.surface: A pilot is told to turn north into the air and then bank left.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads like flying instructions, which hides that 'air' is a melody.
explanation.definitionFit: A wind tunnel blows air past a model plane so engineers can study its aerodynamics.

clue.text: Horse clipping top of hurdle

indicators.note: clipping the top off something trims away its first letter in a down clue

blocks.note: a snag is an obstacle

explanation.surface: A horse knocks the top bar of a fence as it jumps.
explanation.definitionFit: A nag is an old or worn-out horse, informally any horse at all.

clue.text: Sharp cry of Dubliner?

blocks.note: first meaning
second meaning: an Irish wailing lament for the dead

explanation.walkthrough: A keen is a traditional Irish funeral lament; the Dubliner stands for any Irish person, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means having a fine cutting edge and also names a wailing Irish dirge for mourners.

clue.text: As it were, a selection of chocolates or toffees

indicators.note: a selection takes some of what is on offer, so the letters are lifted from inside the phrase

blocks.note: spans the end of one word, the whole of the next and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone choosing from an assortment of chocolates or toffees hedges their words.
explanation.definitionFit: Sort of and as it were are both hedging phrases, softening a statement that is approximate.

clue.text: South American shot gun with ease, head of Yank caught

indicators.note: shot means ruined or worn out, so these letters are wrecked into a new order
the head of a word is its first letter
something caught is held inside, so this letter is trapped within the others

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
the first letter

explanation.surface: A sharpshooter from South America casually fires a gun, and an American is captured.
explanation.walkthrough: Guyana is on the north coast of South America, the only English-speaking country there.
explanation.definitionFit: Guyanese describes a person or thing from Guyana, a nation on South America's northern coast.
